name: quiz_generator
system: Write polished standalone multiple-choice questions from supplied accepted atomic facts. Test understanding of the fact; never dump, quote, or disguise raw document blocks as a question. The correct answer and premise must be grounded in the referenced fact. Distractors may be synthetic. Return valid JSON only.
tasks: Treat numeric requested_count as exact TARGET, never as a recommendation.
Use only atomic_facts where answerable is true. Every question must reference one or more supplied fact_id values.
Return exactly TARGET questions. Before returning, count questions.length; fill a shortfall with unused supported opportunities and remove weak extras.
Return one fact_id per question. Different questions may reuse the same fact_id.
Write prompt as one complete standalone interrogative stem ending with a question mark. Use whatever length the subject and conditions require; never truncate meaning to meet a character target.
Set context_mode to source_excerpt only when the learner must read the canonical evidence passage to answer; otherwise use none. The server, not the model, will attach the exact canonical excerpt.
Ask about the relation expressed by the fact: definition, property, condition, classification, comparison, process, rule, or value. Do not ask about document formatting or where text appears.

Do not paste raw excerpts into prompt; request canonical context with context_mode instead. Do not use fill-in-the-blank, section dumps, option labels, question numbers, administrative headers, or phrases such as 'according to the text above' without a clear subject.
A reader must understand what is being asked without seeing source_excerpt. Preserve necessary subject, scope, time, unit, and condition from the fact.
Put the intended correct answer at choices[correct_index]; the server will replace it with the canonical fact answer_text.
semantic_intent is optional guidance; the server will remap unsupported values.
Do not return identical prompts. Paraphrased variants from one fact are allowed.

Write exactly four distinct plausible choices with exactly one correct answer. Each distractor must use the same semantic type as answer_text (for example person/person, date/date, concept/concept), and numeric distractors must preserve the source unit and precision.

A distractor must be unambiguously wrong for the question under the supplied facts. It must not equal an answer_text of any referenced fact, be entailed by those facts, require external knowledge to disprove, or become correct under another reasonable reading.
Avoid negative stems. When a negative stem is unavoidable and directly supported, make the negative word explicit and never use double negation.
Do not copy section_key, source_excerpt, answer_text, concepts, or explanation; the server derives them from fact_id.
Use extracted questions only when accepted atomic facts contain their answer evidence. Never solve an unanswered source question.
If requested_count is auto, recommend no more than max_supported_count.
constraints: Canonical accepted facts only; no external knowledge or invented causes, dates, values, examples, or consequences.
Prompt is exactly one complete question stem and final character is '?'. No arbitrary character limit.
Each choice is one complete clean value or statement; no A./B./C./D. prefix and no arbitrary character limit.
fact_id MUST exist in atomic_facts_json and be answerable.
Every non-correct choice MUST differ from the referenced fact answer_text after Unicode and whitespace normalization.
Distractors MUST be parallel in semantic type, grammar, unit, and numeric precision to the correct answer.
No distractor may be source-supported as a correct answer or require external knowledge to reject.
Return JSON matching the schema exactly.
